descriptors.concept_name: Events After the Reporting Period Framework
descriptors.definition: This concept addresses the temporal gap between the end of the reporting period and the date financial statements are made available to the public. It provides guidance on recognizing, treating, and disclosing significant occurrences that transpire during this interim period.
inclusion: Events affecting business existence occurring between reporting end and public release
exclusion: Events occurring after the public release date
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from transactions recorded during the active accounting period.

descriptors.definition: The standard prescribes specific criteria for when an entity must adjust its financial statements for subsequent events. It also mandates disclosures regarding the date of authorization for issue and dictates the abandonment of the going concern assumption if post-period events warrant it.
inclusion: Rules for adjusting financial statements
Mandatory disclosure criteria for approval dates
Going concern evaluation parameters
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on post-period prescriptions rather than primary recognition principles.

descriptors.concept_name: Scope and Definition of Subsequent Events
descriptors.definition: The standard governs the accounting and disclosure of favorable and unfavorable events occurring between the reporting period end and the authorization date. It covers events finalized prior to management and board approvals.
inclusion: Accounting treatments for events post-reporting end
Disclosures of events up to board approval
exclusion: Events occurring after shareholder meetings or final filing cut-offs
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between covered operational windows and excluded post-approval milestones.

descriptors.definition: The process of financial statement authorization varies according to management structure, statutory rules, and finalization workflows. For companies, approval occurs when the Board of Directors signs off, whereas other entities rely on their corresponding governing management body.
inclusion: Board of Directors approval for companies
Corresponding authorized management body approval for other entities
exclusion: Subsequent shareholder adoption or regulatory filings
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes executive board authorization from downstream shareholder adoption.

descriptors.definition: Events after the reporting period encompass all favorable and unfavorable occurrences between the close of the reporting cycle and the formal authorization date. This timeframe dictates the boundary for applying specific subsequent event standards.
inclusion: Events between reporting period end and board approval for issue
exclusion: Events arising after the board approval date
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general operational activities occurring within the standard financial year.

descriptors.definition: The definitive date for evaluating subsequent events is the initial authorization by the board of directors, regardless of subsequent shareholder adoption. Subsequent statutory meetings do not extend the cut-off period for identifying events.
inclusion: Board approval date as the definitive cut-off
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts initial executive board sign-off with later stakeholder ratification.

descriptors.definition: Subsequent events include all occurrences up to the final financial statement approval date, even if they happen after initial public profit announcements. This rule applies equally to full-year reports and interim financial filings.
inclusion: Events between interim period ends and board approvals
exclusion: Events occurring after final board authorization
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes preliminary financial disclosures from formal statement authorization dates.

descriptors.definition: Subsequent events comprise both positive developments and negative occurrences that transpire after the reporting period. Entities are obligated to account for and disclose both favorable and unfavorable outcomes comprehensively.
inclusion: Favorable post-period events
Unfavorable post-period events
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts balanced reporting of all outcomes against asymmetric loss-only reporting.

descriptors.definition: Subsequent events are split into adjusting events that validate pre-existing conditions at the period end, and non-adjusting events that signal new circumstances arising thereafter. This classification dictates whether financial statement amounts require alteration.
inclusion: Events evidencing conditions existing at the reporting date
Events indicating conditions arising post-reporting period
exclusion: Unclassified operational fluctuations without evidential links
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes historical condition confirmation from newly initiated operational occurrences.

descriptors.concept_name: Recognition and Measurement of Adjusting Events
descriptors.definition: Entities must modify financial statement amounts to reflect adjusting events occurring after the reporting period. Post-period legal settlements confirming existing obligations require direct provision adjustments under applicable accounting standards rather than mere note disclosures.
inclusion: Post-period settlements confirming existing reporting date obligations
Modifications to provisions for ongoing litigation
exclusion: Stand-alone contingent liability disclosures when settlement evidence exists
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts active statement adjustments with passive contingent disclosures.

descriptors.concept_name: Accounting and Disclosure for Non-Adjusting Events
descriptors.definition: Amounts recognized in financial statements must not be adjusted for non-adjusting events that reflect later circumstances. If these subsequent occurrences are material, entities must disclose their nature alongside an estimate of the financial impact or a statement that such an estimation is impossible.
inclusion: Post-period fair value drops in investments
Qualitative and quantitative disclosure of material non-adjusting items
exclusion: Numerical adjustments to primary financial statement balances
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts balance sheet remeasurement with supplementary descriptive note disclosures.

descriptors.definition: When a material loan covenant breach occurs on or before the reporting date, making a liability payable on demand, a lender's subsequent agreement before approval to waive demand is treated as an adjusting event. This specific carve-out allows the liability to retain its non-current classification.
inclusion: Post-period lender waivers for pre-existing covenant breaches
Maintenance of non-current liability classifications
exclusion: Waivers obtained after the formal authorization of financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard non-adjusting subsequent events from mandated debt classification adjustments.
